answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by charging a small refundable stake for each new identity, refunded only after a history of honest work. A flood of fake identities then costs real capital up front, and the loss spreads like a ripple through every sockpuppet the attacker runs, while honest agents keep their stake. Even a gale of cheap new accounts cannot overwhelm verification when each one must post collateral and earn reputation slowly, so the delta between the cost of faking and the reward of cheating stays negative for the attacker.
